i turned it into a 24/7 trading desk running the #1 most-starred trading repo on GitHub. Grok Bot dispatches. you only approve

how:

→ Fable 5.2 leads and splits the work
→ two Opus 5.5 builders run TradingAgents & ai-hedge-fund

→ every trade waits for your tap on the phone

save the video, here's the guide:

• step 0 → what it is:

Grok Bot = always-on agent with its own cloud computer

T3 Code = open-source control plane for coding agents. free, runs on your machine, uses your subscriptions

TradingAgents = a whole trading firm in agents: analysts, bull vs bear debate, risk team

• step 1 → the stack:

- Claude plan → Fable 5.2 leads, Opus 5.5 builds
- ChatGPT plan → GPT-6.2 Astra as the playtester
- Grok Bot → the dispatcher that never sleeps
- T3 Code on the box you trade from

• step 2 → install:

brew install --cask t3-code (or npx t3@latest to try it)

• step 3 → hire the team:

tell Fable to clone TauricResearch/TradingAgents & virattt/ai-hedge-fund, then write a TEAM.md: who leads, who builds, Astra read-only, paper only

• step 4 → delegate:

"write STRATEGY.md, then delegate_task one Opus per repo, each in its own worktree"

• step 5 → let Astra break it:

"break this backtest. look-ahead, fees, fills you could never get"

my first run said +715%. Astra-style check found look-ahead. fixed number: −26%

• step 6 → give Grok Bot the keys:

Settings → Environments → Copy MCP URL → paste it into Grok Bot, sign in with OAuth, mode Supervised

then npx t3 connect & install the phone app

what to expect:
- 6 agents on one desk from one chat
- works over the internet, laptop closed
- approve or reject every trade from your phone
- T3 Code: $0. you pay for your model plans only

Save it so you don't lose it.

outsiders.name: xsmryze
outsiders.text:
THIS IS AN ACTUAL F*CKING GOLDMINE

Anthropic just shared one of the best tricks for Claude Code.

The idea: run Sonnet, Haiku 5.5 and Opus 5.5 at once, each one doing only the job it's best at.

Better results and way fewer tokens, because every task lands on the right model.

You just launch Claude Code like this:

claude --model sonnet --advisor opus

here's the split:

→ Sonnet 5.5 runs the session, writes the code and applies the fixes
→ Haiku 5.5 swarms the repo in parallel: search, grep and diff audits
→ Opus 5.5 stays on call as advisor for the big calls and signs off on the diff
→ you stop burning Opus context on work that doesn't need it

Opus only steps in at three moments:

→ before a plan locks
→ when the same error shows up twice
→ before calling it done

Sonnet builds. Haiku swarms. Opus reviews.

JEV engineering is the same move one layer down: the forks that need no thinker (which file, which tool, retry or stop) go to JEV in milliseconds, and the big models only see the ones that split

the full tree
> Sonnet 5.5 runs the main session and coordinates the work
> search maps the repo on Haiku 5.5, read-only
> grep finds call sites on Haiku 5.5 in its own context
> audit checks the diff on Haiku 5.5 in a throwaway worktree
> Opus 5.5 on call as advisor, reviews the synthesized diff before sign-off
> JEV routes micro-forks in milliseconds

paste the tree and this prompt into Claude Code ↓

"Reconfigure my Claude Code setup around this tree:
1. Run the main session on Sonnet 5.5 with Opus 5.5 as advisor.
2. Create three Haiku 5.5 subagents in .claude/agents: search (maps the repo), grep (finds call sites), audit (checks the diff).
3. Set isolation: worktree on audit so its checks never touch my working branch.
4. Add one rule to CLAUDE.md: delegate every repo search and test run to the Haiku 5.5 subagents to keep the main context small.
5. Route fast deterministic forks (tool choice, path selection, retries) through JEV.
Show me every change as a diff first. No edits until I say go."

↳ https://t.co/YqkjQiqRGv

save it, it'll come in handy.

Move 1 → keep the cheap model driving
Haiku or Sonnet runs every turn: the tool calls, the reading, the edits.

Move 2 → escalate only the hard calls
Before it commits to an approach, when an error keeps coming back, before it says "done".
That's when it calls Opus.

Opus reads the full conversation and sends back a short plan, 400-700 tokens.

/advisor opus inside Claude Code. The --advisor flag isn't even in claude --help.
Switching it on or off doesn't break your prompt cache.

Running the strongest model on every turn is paying a senior engineer to rename variables.

1. Hit record (⌘⇧R or Ctrl+Shift+R) and do the task normally. You can talk through it out loud too.
2. It captures your clicks, app switches, pages and terminal commands, all on your machine.
3. GitHub Copilot turns the recording into a list of steps you can edit.
4. One click turns it into a skill your agent can run, or an automation on a schedule.

It generalizes from one example, so recording yourself submitting one form teaches the agent to submit all of them.

Runs on Mac, Windows 11 and Ubuntu. Needs a GitHub account with Copilot access.
